title: Isolate metrics collector, add CI flakiness guardrails, and incremental snapshot comparator
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: Our performance regression and load harness has accumulated several classes of flakiness and coupling that make CI runs slow and noisy. Two recurring root causes are: (1) the in-process metrics collector and aggregator adds GC/lock noise to runner processes, and (2) the snapshot comparator operates as a full-file comparison that causes massive golden-set churn for small, localizable regressions. This ticket scopes a refactor to (A) extract and isolate the metrics collector into a sidecar/worker process with a stable ingest protocol, (B) add CI guardrails to reduce nondeterministic test failures, and (C) replace the monolithic comparator with an incremental comparator that reports fine-grained diffs and supports per-metric thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Metrics collector runs as an independent process (sidecar or service) for local/CI/integration runs and exposes the same telemetry schema used in production
CI flakiness rate for perf regression and load tests (measured as red-to-green within 24h) reduced by >= 60% during the 2-week observation window
Incremental snapshot comparator integrated into the regression pipeline with per-metric tolerances and a human-friendly report; comparator run time reduced by >= 50% on typical goldenset
Documentation updated: runbook for troubleshooting metrics drift, migration guide for local devs, and CI config examples
steps: Design: define telemetry v2 schema and transport protocol (gRPC/HTTP) for collector sidecar
Spike: prototype a Rust-based sidecar that accepts proto-packed metrics and writes normalized protobufs to S3 for later aggregation
Comparator: implement incremental comparator that ingests streaming metrics and computes delta with threshold rules
CI changes: add deterministic seeding, retry-budget policy, and 'snapshot gate' job that blocks rollouts on high-variance signals
Dependency upgrades: bump opentelemetry to 1.10, prometheus_client to 0.15, pytest to 8.x; verify compatibility
Instrumentation: add trace hooks and sample-mode on sidecar to avoid sampling storms during full regression runs
Docs and runbooks: migration guide for local devs and example Docker Compose for sidecar-based local runs
updates: 2026-02-19: Kickoff meeting with Perf, Infra, and DX. Agreed scope and measurable SLO (60% flakiness reduction).
2026-02-24: Design doc posted to Confluence. Telemetry schema v2 (fields & cardinality) approved by Infra. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/Perf/metrics-collector-v2

2026-03-02: Spike complete — prototype sidecar accepts UDP/HTTP metrics and writes normalized protobufs to staging bucket. Preliminary numbers: 12-18% lower GC latency in runner process under synthetic load.
2026-03-06: Implemented deterministic seeding option in synthetic runner and added environment flag PERF_DETERMINISTIC=true. CI pipeline updated on a branch for validation.
2026-03-10: Comparator PoC produces incremental diffs; end-to-end run time on goldenset reduced by ~52% on CI runners. Open PRs: GH #2271, GH #2283.
2026-03-12: Security and infra review scheduled for 2026-03-15 (sidecar network policy and bucket ACLs).
comments: Jaspreet Kaur (Infra): We need to validate that sidecar memory footprint stays under 120MB for our CI pool sizes. If not, we have to add a lightweight aggregator mode.
Marta Rivera (DX): Local developer experience must remain simple; provide a single docker-compose up that brings sidecar + runner for iteration.
Rohit Patel (Perf): Worth adding a 'smoke deterministic' profile that runs on PRs to catch gross regressions without full goldenset cost.
Code review (Liam): GH #2271 has feedback about the proto name collision; prefer metrics.v2.Record over MetricsRecord to avoid future migration friction.
estimated_cost_savings: ~20% per-regression-run token compute and CI minutes for full goldenset runs
qa_checklist: Run full regression goldenset in staging with sidecar enabled and compare to baseline run (same commit)
Validate deterministic-seed runs for 50 consecutive CI builds with zero nondeterministic deltas
Confirm sidecar memory/CPU usage within budget on smallest Dedicated CI instance
Verify incremental comparator reports per-metric thresholds and produces human-digestible HTML report
risks_mitigation: Risk: sidecar adds deployment complexity and network overhead. Mitigation: start with an 'in-process shim' mode that uses the same ingestion API but emits to local socket; only flip to sidecar after 2-week staging validation. Risk: dependency upgrades break legacy adapters — mitigation: run compatibility matrix and keep adapter compatibility layer for 1 release cycle.
notes: This ticket intentionally avoids changing the production telemetry ingestion path; goal is to stabilize test harness signals first, then consider back-propagation to production collectors in a follow-up. Coordinate with Release WG for a rollout window where we can afford a 24-hour observation period.
